lines.text: sorrow long for freedom. The love of God which takes us not
as those who we now are and into whom we have made
ourselves, but as those who we are not, who we ought and
wish to be, who we shall be. And by this means the divine
love makes that which we are, apparent only, and bestows
in its stead our genuine and true life.
This love of God is not a goal towards which we strive—
who could ever obtain it by striving?-but it is the power
which already enclasps and enfolds us, and to which our
eyes have only to be opened; and we are to turn our gaze
and our meditation on Him in whom it has appeared
incarnate, Jesus Christ. To know oneself to be sustained by
this love means to be free from the bondage of the past, from
the fetters of oneself, free for the future which God will
bestow and for the glory which shall be revealed to us.
This freedom creates in us the hope of which Paul says:
"For in this hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is
not hope. For who hopes for what he sees?" Hope focuses
itself on the invisible, on that of which we can have no
conception or imagination. But this hope must be enter-
tained in patience: "But if we hope for what we do not see,
we wait for it with patience." This no doubt requires always
new power and self-conquest. But if we are aware of the
love of God we belong to those who have the "first fruits of
the Spirit", i.e. those in whose present life the power of the
future is effectually shown. And the Spirit "helps us in our
weakness". When we feel our own powers enteebled, then
the power of God intervenes to help us, and our confession
that in our own strength we can do nothing, becomes a
prayer.
For what are we to pray? "We do not know how to pray
as we ought"—we have of course all our multifarious
wishes for the future, but in the presence of God they must
be silent. And when all our conscious aims for the future are
transcended and our way in life from a human point of view
seems to be without a goal, when only our longing and
aspiration remain, then in this very longing, unknown to
ourselves, there speaks the voice of the Spirit. "The Spirit
